en: Ah, all right. I'm very sorry.
That logic is odd. Older woman all used to be girls at some point. Or are you saying you're not going to be an older woman yourself someday?
That's not it. Old ladies are from the past. The young girls of today aren't gonna be old ladies when they grow up.
Then what are they going to be?
I dunno. Old ladies are old ladies. People's personalities don't change as they age.
So, shouldn't there be girls who are headstrong even when they're young?
Yeah, but headstrong old ladies are a product of a different generation. We younger girls are all totally normal!
We're back to that again? Geez, you really are a stubborn one.
Specialty shops?
Yeah. Some offer all-you-can-eat, and Oita style karaage is pretty popular now, too. I hear Oita prefecture consumes the most amount of chicken in Japan.
Really? Is it any different from normal karaage?
Oita's karaage is famous for its strong flavor. It uses soy sauce or salt as a base for a spicy marinade that includes ginger and garlic.
Wow, I'll hafta give it a try sometime! All-you-can-eat karaage sounds super delicious!
Maybe we can go sometime.
Not sometime! I wanna have some now! Ya got me all in the mood for fatty food, Akiyama-san!
Aren't you always in that mood?
Right, but how does this all-you-can-eat work? How much does it cost a la carte?
Uh... I don't know that much about it.
Well, I'm the kinda gal who eats a ton at buffets to get my money's worth. I like to try at least one a' everythin'.
You really are stingy.
I'm a big fan of exclusive dishes and desserts, with limited availability. If a theme park has a special tastin' menu, then I always go.
Hmm. That does sound kind of fun.
I'm fine with all-you-can-eat, but all-you-can-drink is no good. I'm not drinkin' for a while.
You don't have to drink just because they have an all-you-can-drink option.
Akiyama-san, we already talked about this.
No way. Did we really?
Don't ya know any other interestin' topics?
Did you know that comedians hang out at the Watami here in Sotenbori?
Apparently, they go there after live performances, for an afterparty.
Wow, I had no idea! I wonder if I could get a handshake if I went to go see 'em?
Well, it's more of a postmortem than a party. They seem really serious, so it's difficult for fans to approach them during that time.
I see. Comedians are all pretty serious, actually. But I still kinda wanna check 'em out.
They're not there all the time, but your chances of running into them are pretty high if you hang out around there.
Really? I've hit up plenty a' school mixers at that Watami, but I've never managed to meet a comedian.
Even if they're there, they might not pay any attention to other customers. You might not have noticed them.
Wow. Comedians are real pros. I couldn't deal with havin' an after work postmortem meetin'.
Even things that seem glamorous usually have some kind of harsh reality on the flipside. There's no success without hard work, after all.
Maybe I oughta do postmortems too. Like, "A customer didn't wanna get a bottle today!"
I don't know. I'm not sure the customers would appreciate that level of scrutiny.
Ya know, I'm a fast talker, but those comedians can talk even faster.
And they're still easy to understand. They don't even trip over their words.
I'm sooo jealous! I wonder what it takes to be able to speak so skillfully?
Maybe the secret lies in those postmortem meetings they have.
Yeah, but I dunno if I wanna go out drinkin' again right now. I don't wanna lose another coat.
You do know you can go to a place that serves alcohol and not drink, right?
I hear nonalcoholic cocktails are popular now.
Non-alcoholic?
Yeah. In addition to having no alcohol, they also have no calories and no sugar.
So you can drink way more than regular cocktails, without getting drunk or gaining weight. They're the perfect thing for a girls' night out.
Wow, they make stuff like that?
But I think it's fun to get kinda drunk and get my spirits up! I dunno if nonalcoholic drinks would fit the bill.
Well, if you get the chance, it might be fun to try one.
Maybe they're good for new students. A lot of them are still minors, y'know?
Yeah, good point. It's no good to push liquor on people who are underage.
Maybe I'll whip up some of these nonalcoholic cocktails for the new students next year!
Speakin' of, I heard yer alcohol tolerance is connected to your blood type.
Really? I think there's too much personal variance for that to be the case.
I think so too, but what if it's true?
At any rate, you should still try not to drink too much.
Oh yeah, if there's no alcohol, I probably wouldn't black out and lose my memory.
Of course. If you still lose your memory with nonalcoholic drinks, you've got other issues.
I'll hafta try 'em out sometime! I do hate losin' my coat.
I get too nervous to talk around someone I like, so I gotta rely on the booze for help.
Liquid courage, huh?
Yep. Non-alcoholic drinks won't get me drunk, so it'd be embarrassin' to say stuff while I'm sober.
That's kind of cute, in a way.
Did you know that okonomiyaki is good for people who are dieting?
No way! That stuff's gotta make you fat! Doesn't it?
Depends on what you put in it. Wheat flour itself is low in fat and packed with protein, vitamins, and minerals.
Cabbage is nutritious and low-calorie, and pork is full of vitamin B1. The sauce doesn't even have oil in it, so it's low in calories too.
Really? But on menus that show calories, I feel like it's usually pretty high up there.
That's probably from fatty cuts of pork or mayonnaise. Yakisoba, cheese, and mochi can also bump up the calorie count, I hear.
As long as you don't use those ingredients, you can have a low-calorie, nutritious meal that's great for someone who's on a diet.
Wow, I had no idea! It's easy to make at home too, so maybe I'll give it a shot sometime!
Yeah, being able to make it at home is nice.
I was cravin' pork skewers, but now I'm kinda feelin' like okonomiyaki, too.
You sure love heavy foods. Make sure to keep the ingredients in mind if you're going to be doing this for your diet.
Hey, when my brother gets home, I should bust out the griddle and make some okonomiyaki!
Oh, homemade okonomiyaki sounds nice. I bet you'll even become friends with his girlfriend.
Huh? I'm not really thinkin' about that...
The other day, I went to an okonomiyaki place and got 'em to throw in toppin's for free!
Wow. I'm guessing you haggled them into it?
Of course! Eatin' out is just like shoppin'!
I'm not sure why I even asked...
I get impatient when I'm cookin' on a hotpot or the griddle, and I don't like other folks messin' with me.
I definitely get that impression.
Okonomiyaki lets me fix things up the way I want it. If someone else takes charge of it before it's ready to eat, I kinda snap.
Yikes. If I ever go out to eat with you, I'll have to make sure I don't interfere.
I wonder what this year's fashion trends are...
Dunno. If I see somethin' I like in the store, I just buy it. I don't consider what's in vogue or not.
During the fall and winter of last year, British fashions and '60s classics were popular.
Oh yeah! Girls are probably still wearing 'em this year, too. I just like lots of colorful clothing!
Seems like a lot of girls have their own fashion taste, regardless of the current trends.
Ya sure know lots about ladies' fashion, Akiyama-san! I'm kinda surprised.
I just see so many cute girls out there, it comes naturally.
Stores raise the prices on stuff that's in fashion, so ya gotta haggle over it! Maybe it's better to wait until it gets cheaper.
No, if something's in fashion, it'll sell out pretty fast. So if you don't buy it when you see it, you may not be able to get your hands on it again.
That ain't true! Once the season ends, they usually have clearance sales. That's where ya find the best bargains!
But aren't those just the items that weren't popular, and never became fashionable in the first place?
As a '90s Heisei girl myself, I'm shocked by '60s and Showa-era fashion in general.
When I see old footage on TV, I just gotta wonder what they were thinkin'!
You do realize at the beginning of the Heisei era, fashions from the '80s bubble era were still around, right?
Really? I don't remember back that far. I know that those baggy socks were already outta fashion when I was in grade school.
Wow. Just hearing that makes me feel like an old man.
See, bringin' that up is just remindin' me of my coat all over again! Ugh, I'm still really upset 'bout the whole thing...
Sorry. I shouldn't have brought it up.
Speakin' of which, I met a great guy the other day, but his fashion sense was the pits. That turned me off right away.
How was he dressed when you first saw him?
He was wearin' a suit. Looked like a hard-workin' businessman. I was hoodwinked!
A suit makes things a lot easier for men. Guess even us guys need to be hip to fashion.
What sort of things do you like, Honoka-chan? I'm kind of curious.
What do ya mean?
What foods do you like?
I'm a fan of meat!
Well, meat can mean a number of different things, like beef or pork.
As long as it's meat I'm good. Even chicken or horse.
Horse? That's unusual. But that's good to know. I can invite you out to eat basically anywhere.
Oh, but fish is a no go.
Can't handle it? Why not?
I'm not so great with chopsticks, so it makes a real big mess when I try to eat it.
Yeah, there aren't very many people who can eat fish neatly with chopsticks, I don't think.
That's why I don't eat it in front of a guy. I don't wanna disappoint him.
You've given this a lot of thought.
Fish is good for you. It's full of DHA, so it's good for the brain.
Wait, is that yer roundabout way of sayin' I'm dumb?
No, I wasn't trying to imply that at all.
Then what did ya mean by it?
Just that it's better to not be a fussy eater.
It ain't like I hate it or nothin'. I was just sayin' I don't like to eat it around others.
Ugh, look at what ya did. Now I'm all ticked off.
What kind of music do you usually listen to?
Music, huh? Lemme think...
I usually listen to the radio, but not music.
Radio?
Yeah, like shows that comedians host. They take a lotta really fun joke submissions from listeners.
Ah, so late-night programming then. Comedy on radio is different than on TV, huh? It's fun because you can use your imagination more.
Yeah, you get what I mean! I can tell ya about all sortsa funny shows out there!
I'll have to give them a listen.
What would you like most right now?
That's an easy one! Cold. Hard. Cash.
I mean if someone were to give you a present.
Then I'd want it to be money.
Right, but if you did get money, what would you buy with it? Then it'd be like you'd gotten that as a present in the first place.
Nah, it ain't that. If I got money, the fun part is figurin' out what to buy with it.
When I want somethin', I like the satisfaction of bein' able to buy it myself. Gettin' it from someone else just doesn't give me that same feelin'.
I see your reasoning, sure. But what would you like to go buy right now if you could?
Oooh, that's a secret!
What are your hobbies, Honoka-chan?
Hobbies? Lately, I've been into people watchin'.
People watching, huh? I've met girls who are into that sort of thing. What do you enjoy about it?
When I gotta kill time waitin' on a friend or something, I look around and watch other folks waitin' and guess what kinda person they are.
That does sound fun. Are you ever right?
I think it's more fun if I ain't right.
Oh? Meaning what, exactly?
Like if some cute girl's waitin', I usually imagine she's waitin' for a hot guy.
And then some ugly dude'll show up and I'll be like, "What the heck!?" I find mismatches like that real fun!
Haha. I bet that scenario happens in reverse, too.
Yep! Then I talk to my friends about how he's gotta be payin' her, and that he's probably goin' to jail.
If the person you're waiting for shows up, maybe you should be on your way.
Sounds dull. All you do is sit and watch?
Well, what sorta stuff are you into, Akiyama-san?
Me? If I saw a girl like that waiting on someone, I might go chat her up and ask her out to get coffee or something.
Ew, gross! That's just bein' a pick-up artist!
If you make sure to pick the right person, they might be quite happy to come along.
